name: National Bushing & Parts Co
old_description: Since 1920, National Bushing & Parts Company has served professional installers and serious do-it-yourself customers throughout Minnesota with quality parts, supplies and service. During the 1990s, the National Bushing name transitioned to the Auto Value banner. Today, there are more than 160 company stores and independent store customers throughout Minnesota, North Dakota, Wisconsin and Michigan.
about:
National Bushing & Parts Co. traces its roots to 1920 when Ray Riley and Aime Pouliot founded the company in Minneapolis, Minnesota. The pair began by manufacturing bronze bushings and distributing replacement parts for early automobiles such as Pierce Arrow, Packard, and Ford, as well as truck, bus, and tractor components. In the 1990s the National Bushing name transitioned to the Auto Value banner, and the business is now headquartered in Mora, Minnesota, under the ownership of the Bartlett family, which has led the company for three generations.

Today the company operates as Automotive Parts Headquarters (APH), a wholesale distributor serving a network of more than 160 company stores and independent store customers across Minnesota, North Dakota, Wisconsin, and Michigan. A 160,000-square-foot distribution center in St. Cloud, opened in 2006, supports warehousing and logistics for the Auto Value brand. APH has been a member of the Aftermarket Auto Parts Alliance since 1986, leveraging the coalition’s purchasing power and branding.

The customer base includes professional installers and serious do-it-yourself buyers seeking automotive aftermarket parts, supplies, and service. Historically the catalog covered components for passenger cars, trucks, buses, and tractors; the current offering spans the full range of aftermarket repair parts sold through the Auto Value retail network.

The company’s early reputation for machine-shop expertise and a diverse inventory helped it become one of the upper Midwest’s leading parts wholesalers. Leadership emphasizes carefully designed growth strategies and the strength of the Alliance affiliation, which the Bartlett family credits for sustaining expansion well into the future.
